_note: Approximate, illustrative port-infrastructure reference data for the FreightSight AI demo. Updated 2026-09-11 across two research passes: draft/berth figures re-checked against current port-authority, government and news sources for every one of the 18 ports. Entries WITHOUT a 'last_verified' field (Nacala, Beira, Samarinda, Taboneo) had no confirmed recent infrastructure change found and still reflect the original illustrative estimate -- verify with the port authority / IHS-Markit before production use.

Newcastle.notes: World's largest coal export port; frequent queueing at anchorage. Port-wide there are 20 operational berths across all terminals (coal + general cargo); the 'berths' figure below is left as the legacy coal-terminal-specific estimate pending confirmation of the current dedicated coal-berth count.
Newcastle.verification_source: Wikipedia/Port Authority of NSW port profile

Gladstone.notes: Coal and bauxite export hub. Port-wide there are 20 operational berths (Gladstone Ports Corporation); a sailing draft of ~17 m is generally available from the deep-draft export terminals, subject to tide. New container-terminal development (ROI opened Oct 2025) also underway.
Gladstone.verification_source: Maritime Safety Queensland Port of Gladstone port procedures manual (Apr 2025); GPC container-terminal ROI announcement (Oct-Nov 2025)

Hay Point.notes: Deep-water coal terminal, Capesize-capable; two terminals at the port -- Dalrymple Bay Coal Terminal (4 berths, ~85 MTPA) and Hay Point Coal Terminal (2 berths, ~55 MTPA) -- combine for 6 berths and ~99.5 Mt/yr of coal exports.
Hay Point.verification_source: ShipNext/marinelink port profile; Dalrymple Bay Infrastructure / GEM terminal profiles

Norfolk.notes: Major US East Coast coal export terminal. Norfolk Harbor's federal channel was deepened to 55 ft (16.8 m) under the Port of Virginia's $450M 'Wider, Deeper, Safer' program -- dredging substantially complete Feb 2026, formally inaugurated Jun 2026 -- making it the deepest commercial shipping channel on the US East Coast.
Norfolk.verification_source: Virginia Port Authority/USACE project completion coverage (WorkBoat, ProfessionalMariner, WVTF), Feb-Jun 2026

Baltimore.notes: Chesapeake Bay approach draft-limits vessel size. The Fort McHenry Federal Channel was fully blocked by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse (26 Mar 2024) and reopened to its original 700 ft / 50 ft (15.2 m) dimensions on 11 Jun 2024 -- no lasting change to channel draft. The bridge itself is still under reconstruction (targeted for 2028).

Nacala.notes: Deep natural harbour; Vale/Moatize coal corridor.

Beira.notes: Shallow, silted approach channel; Handysize/Supramax only.

Vostochny.notes: Pacific coast coal terminal; sanctions/logistics-driven schedule risk. An approved berth-reconstruction project targets 16.5-18 m depth at berths 51/52 (19 m in the approach channel/turning area) as part of a capacity increase toward 70 MTPA -- but a firm completion date could not be confirmed this session, so the 'max_draft_m' figure below is left at the original illustrative estimate pending confirmation.
Vostochny.verification_source_note: Project found (CoalHub coverage of approved reconstruction), but completion status unconfirmed as of 2026-09-11 -- not marked last_verified.

Murmansk.notes: Ice-free Arctic port; winter weather delay risk. A new, separate deep-water coal terminal, Lavna (western Kola Bay, ~18 MTPA capacity, expandable to 24 MTPA, ~15 m depth near shore), began commercial coal exports in Mar 2025 -- but has run well below capacity (600,000 t in its first 7 months) amid weak regional coal-export demand. Figures below still describe the original Murmansk Commercial Sea Port terminal.
Murmansk.verification_source: Barents Observer/Interfax/CCA coal-market coverage of Lavna port launch, Mar 2025 - 2026

Samarinda.notes: River port; deeper vessels load via ship-to-ship transfer offshore.

Taboneo.notes: Anchorage transshipment point off Kalimantan; barge-fed.

Paradip.notes: Deepest East Coast port; inner-harbour capital dredging to 18.5 m completed Aug 2026, enabling fully-laden Capesize berthing at Western Dock-1 (first Capesize call: Sep 2026). Mechanised-berth share ~80%, targeting 100% by 2030.
Paradip.verification_source: MoPSW/PPA project inauguration coverage (The Week, Maritime Gateway, Hellenic Shipping News), Aug-Sep 2026

Visakhapatnam.notes: Outer harbour dredged to 18.1 m draft for Capesize/Super-Cape berthing; inner harbour separately limited to ~14.5 m (Panamax). Outer harbour handles large bulkers; frequent congestion.
Visakhapatnam.verification_source: Vizag Port Authority allowable-drafts circular; MoPSW port-technology coverage

Gangavaram.notes: India's deepest all-weather private port; Phase II expansion (completed 2016) brought it to 9 berths and ~64 MTPA capacity, incl. 2 mechanised coal berths handling Capesize vessels up to 200,000 DWT. Draft cited 18-21 m depending on berth.
Gangavaram.verification_source: Wikipedia/GEM port profile cross-checked against Adani Ports Phase-II completion release

Gopalpur.notes: Deep-draft, direct-berthing multi-cargo port between Paradip and Visakhapatnam; grew from 1 to 3 berths (800 m quay, ~15 m depth, 20 MTPA) well past the original lighterage-port figures. Acquired by Adani Ports (APSEZ) in Mar 2024; a further concession worth Rs 16,554 crore was signed Jun 2025 targeting ~50 MTPA capacity.
Gopalpur.verification_source: CBInsights/Deccan Herald/EPC World Gopalpur Port acquisition and expansion coverage, 2024-2025

Dhamra.notes: Deep-draft mechanised coal/iron-ore terminal; approach channel 18 km, dredged for up to 180,000 DWT vessels. Cargo capacity has grown well past the original 25 MTPA (2 berths) toward a 100+ MTPA target as Adani's phased expansion (plan: 13-14 berths by ~2020s, 35 berths / 300 MTPA long-term) proceeds; exact current operational berth count could not be confirmed from public sources this session -- treat 'berths' below as a lower bound pending port-authority confirmation.
Dhamra.verification_source: Wikipedia port infobox; Adani Ports/GEM Dhamra Port profile (conflicting berth-count reporting, flagged)

Sagar Sandheads.notes: Open-sea transshipment anchorage; motherships lighter into barges for Kolkata/Haldia dock. No draft limit for anchorage itself, but slow transshipment throughput causes idle time. A separate deep-sea 'Sagar Port' project (targeting ~10.5-13.5 m alongside depth) remains in development/funding stages as of this check -- not yet an operating berthed facility, so it hasn't changed the anchorage's own operating profile.
Sagar Sandheads.verification_source: Wikipedia Sagar Port project status check, 2026

Haldia.notes: Riverine dock, tide-dependent; Handysize/Supramax only, larger parcels need Sagar transshipment. Port-wide there are 12 berths across 6 wharves (Syama Prasad Mukherjee Port Authority); the legacy '2 berths' figure understated the current facility.
Haldia.verification_source: Wikipedia Haldia Dock Complex infobox (FY2025-26 cargo/berth data)
